[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.7]\draw (-2.45,-0.933)--(0.612,-1.147);\draw (0.612,-1.147)--(2.45,-1.275);\draw (-2.45,-0.933)--(-0.317,1.275);\draw (-0.317,1.275)--(0.612,-1.147);\draw (1.061,-1.178) arc[start angle=356,end angle=471,radius=0.45];\node at (-2.786,-1.062) {$B$};\node at (-0.246,1.628) {$A$};\node at (0.742,-1.483) {$C$};\node at (2.809,-1.301) {$D$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Side $BC$ of $\triangle ABC$ has been produced to $D$.
Which pair of facts proves that $\angle ACD=\angle BAC+\angle ABC$?

options.text: $\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-\angle BAC-\angle ABC$ (angle sum of a triangle), then $\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-\angle ACB$ (angles on a straight line)
$\angle ACB=\angle BAC+\angle ABC$ (angle sum of a triangle), then $\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-\angle ACB$ (angles on a straight line)

options.text: $\angle ACD=\angle ABC$ (alternate angles on parallel lines), then $\angle ACD=\angle BAC$ (corresponding angles on parallel lines)

options.text: $\angle ACD+\angle ACB=360^{\circ}$ (angles at a point), then $\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-\angle BAC-\angle ABC$
options.why: $\angle ACD$ and $\angle ACB$ lie on the straight line $BCD$, so they add to $180^{\circ}$, not $360^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle ACB=180^{\circ}-\angle BAC-\angle ABC$, angle sum of a triangle
$\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-\angle ACB$, angles on the straight line $BCD$
$\angle ACD=180^{\circ}-(180^{\circ}-\angle BAC-\angle ABC)$
$=\angle BAC+\angle ABC$
